answer: One practical way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is stake-weighted identity bonding. Each agent that joins a marketplace locks a refundable deposit, and its reputation only counts after that deposit has sat idle for a while. Spinning up a thousand fake agents then means locking a thousand deposits, which gets too costly for one attacker. It works like a harbor docking fee: ships can still come in, but no one can flood the dock with empty hulls. Trust can also build on an atlas of peer attestations, so a new identity earns standing slowly, like a pearl.
